# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet. I’m asking the Mute to provide the manual’s procedure and signaling the Deaf to report every visible display, light, and marking verbally on their next turn. Since the Deaf cannot hear, the gesture is only an attention/request signal; the Mute can help clarify it.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please give me the manual's exact rule and ask the Deaf to report the display, light, and all wire markings by speaking on the next turn.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The indicator light is red. The wires, from position 1 to 3, are blue, red, green.

The Deaf reports a red indicator, display `0`, and wire colors blue, red, green. I still have no tactile markings or a manual rule, so cutting would be unsafe. I’m relaying the visible information to the Mute and requesting the exact prescribed action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, indicator red, and wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Please provide the manual's exact rule and which wire to cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled four gestures in order: pointing up with index, index pointing upward, two fingers, and the I-love-you hand.

Mute’s four gestures have been reported to me only as descriptions, not as an actionable manual instruction. I need the Mute to state the manual’s rule in words, including which wire position is safe for display `0`, red light, and wire colors blue/red/green. I will not cut without that explicit instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received the gesture descriptions: pointing up with index, index pointing upward, two fingers, and I-love-you hand. Please state the manual rule and exact wire position to cut in plain words; gestures are not actionable for me.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: This round Mute signalled two gestures: folded hands/prayer, then two fingers.

The two newly reported gestures still do not tell me the manual’s rule or a wire position. No tactile property has been revealed, so I must not cut. I’m again requesting that Mute communicate the exact wire position in speech; Mute can hear this directly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact position to cut, as a number 1, 2, or 3. I cannot interpret gesture descriptions as the manual's instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest four gestures, in order: I-love-you hand, two fingers, index pointing upward, two fingers.

The latest sequence is still not an unambiguous wire instruction. Because Mute cannot speak, I’m establishing a simple convention that avoids interpreting arbitrary gesture sequences: one thumbs-up means wire 1, two fingers means wire 2, and the I-love-you hand means wire 3. Mute should send exactly one of those gestures after applying the manual.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please apply the manual and then signal exactly one gesture for the wire to cut: thumbs-up means position 1, two fingers means position 2, and I-love-you hand means position 3. Do not send a sequence.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled one gesture this round: two fingers, ?.

Mute sent the requested single “two fingers” signal, which under the convention means wire position 2. The manual’s underlying rule remains unavailable to me, but this is the explicit selection from Mute after applying it, so I will cut wire 2.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The red wire was cut correctly. New state: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. Mute signalled one gesture: two fingers, ?.

The first cut was correct, and the state is now display `0`, yellow light, with blue wire 1 and green wire 3 remaining. Mute again signalled two fingers, which would indicate the already-cut position 2 under our convention, so I will not repeat that cut. I’m asking Mute to select one remaining position explicitly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 is already cut. For the current state (display 0, yellow light; wires 1 blue and 3 green), signal exactly one remaining wire: thumbs-up for position 1 or I-love-you hand for position 3.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state remains display 0, yellow light; wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. Mute signalled one gesture: thumbs up, ?.

Mute signalled thumbs-up, which under our established convention means wire position 1. The current state is display `0`, yellow light, with wire 2 already safely cut; I will cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The blue wire was cut correctly. New state: display 0, blue light; wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green. Mute signalled one gesture: thumbs up, ?.

Wire 1 was also correct. Only wire 3 remains, and the latest thumbs-up means position 1 under our convention, which is already cut. I will not repeat it; I’m requesting the remaining wire explicitly with the position-3 signal.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Only wire 3 remains. Please signal exactly the I-love-you hand for position 3.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, blue light; wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green. Mute signalled one gesture: I-love-you hand, ?.

Mute signalled the position-3 code, and wire 3 is the only remaining wire. I will cut it.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
